## CSI 300 Slides 8.5% in October as Beijing Weighs Stock Support


The People's Bank of China is set to meet the National Financial Regulatory Administration, the China Securities Regulatory Commission and major banks on Monday, according to[investingLive](https://investinglive.com/stock-market-update/china-s-central-bank-regulators-to-meet-on-stock-support-after-record-12-week-slide/) , citing a Sunday report by Cailian that quoted industry people. The agenda is reported to be improving a relending programme that funds share buybacks and stake increases, under which companies and major shareholders borrow from banks backed by central bank funding to buy shares.


The 21st Century Business Herald reported that some securities firms and funds had been notified, investingLive said, though there has been no official confirmation of the agenda or of any planned measures. The CSI 300 fell 8.5% in October and entered a[bear market](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/bull-market-vs-bear-market-definition-examples-and-how-it-compares/) , its record 12th straight weekly decline and its worst month in more than a decade, per the same report.


Measures announced in October did not stop the losses, with weak domestic growth and doubts over AI earnings weighing on investors, investingLive reported. In its view, only a meaningful expansion of the relending programme would signal real firepower, while a credible package could ease pressure on the yuan and support Asian risk appetite.

## PBOC Makes the 1.25% Overnight Rate Its Policy Anchor


Per[The Standard](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/347048/Chinas-central-bank-steps-up-shift-toward-overnight-rate-as-policy-anchor) , carrying Reuters, the daily overnight operations are fixed-rate, quantity-based tenders, and the 1.25% operating rate was disclosed for the first time. The seven-day reverse repo shifts to a fixed-quantity tender with multiple winning bid rates, run mainly around tax payment periods and month-ends.


Other tools, such as temporary repo and reverse repo operations, will be priced at a spread to the overnight rate, with spread sizes unchanged, the report said. PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said earlier in October that the bank was studying a switch of its main policy rate to the overnight reverse repo rate.


Zhou Hao, chief economist at Guotai Junan International, described the move this way, according to the report:


> "The clearest signal yet that the PBOC is moving toward an overnight-rate-based operating system."


Ming Ming, chief economist at Citic Securities, said the reform of the short-end mechanism lays groundwork for diversifying the benchmarks for loan rates and for passing broad interest rate declines through to the economy, The Standard reported.
